subject: URGENT: 5xx/429 surge for FinSight - gateway auth misclassifying JWT failures
messages:
From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@finsight.io>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-team@finsight.io
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: High 5xx/429 for our tenant — production impact

Jonas,

We started seeing a spike in 5xx and 429 responses to our production calls around 06:30 PST this morning. Page fired twice — average p99 latency jumped to ~2.4s and a subset of requests are failing with 502/503 and 429. Our retries are making it worse; we suspect a retry storm. This is hitting our ingestion pipeline and causing backpressure.

Attached is a small support_log_snippet.txt and a PCAP capture from our gateway for the 06:30-07:15 window. Can you confirm whether this was on Redwood's side or our config? We are escalating internally and need an ETA on mitigation.

Thanks,
Tom
SRE, FinSight Analytics

----

Attachment: gateway-trace-20260220.pcap (pcap)

Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 08:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 for our tenant — production impact

Tom —

Thanks for the data; we've ingested the logs. We're triaging now. Early signal from our edge logs shows a concentrated spike of token validation failures that our gateway is surfacing as 5xx/429 instead of 401/403 in a few code paths. That would explain the retry amplification.

Immediate plan:
- I'm convening infra and runtime teams (CCed) and we'll pull detailed traces.
- We will instrument a short-lived rule to return 401 for auth failures (if safe) and a circuit-breaker on the tenant to stop retries for 15m.
- ETA for initial mitigation: 45–60 mins.

Can you confirm whether your clients have clock sync issues or aggressive retries? Any latest deploys on your side?

I'll follow up with a timeline.

—Jonas
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 for our tenant — production impact

TECH UPDATE (internal) — evidence summary:
- Edge/gateway logs (06:28:14–06:35:02): sharp rise in TokenValidationService errors: "token_decode_error: invalid_nbf" and "clock_skew_validation_failed". These are surfaced upstream as generic 502/503 in our gateway adapter when downstream auth service timed out.
- Root cause hypothesis: A transient clock skew on several FinSight instances caused JWT 'nbf' (not-before) checks to fail; their clients then retried with exponential backoff but with insufficient cap causing a retry pile-up.
- We observed a correlated spike in upstream auth service latency (auth-svc p95 from 20ms to 1.2s), likely due to burst of validation requests from retries.

Mitigations applied at 09:18 PST:
1) Short-circuit: mapped auth validation failures to 401 for tenant FS-4782 for 20 minutes.
2) Tenant-level token-throttle: rate-limit validation calls to auth-svc per-tenant to reduce load.
3) Push emergency flag to routing plane to favor fallback model variant in the Dedicated pool for their route.

Next: pending logs from FinSight confirming their client clocks; evaluate whether we should add explicit 401 mapping globally for token validation failure classes.

-Dev

From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@finsight.io>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-team@finsight.io, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 10:13:00 -0800
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 for our tenant — production impact

Thanks for the fast response. We confirmed several autoscaled ingestion workers had their NTP daemon briefly misconfigured after a container restart; clocks were ~7s behind. We also had a sudden increase in concurrent retries after our ingestion backoff threshold was hit.

We've re-synced clocks and pushed a fix. After your short-circuit and throttles, our error rate dropped by ~85% within 12 minutes. Attached is a screenshot (slo-heatmap-finsight.png) that shows the p99 drop.

Please confirm whether Redwood will convert token-validation gateway failures to 401/403 in the future to avoid misclassification and retry storms.

-Tom

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@finsight.io>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Final update — root cause, customer impact, and follow-ups

Summary for execs and FinSight:  
- Root cause: transient NTP/config issue on FinSight instances produced JWT 'nbf' and 'clock skew' validation failures. Our gateway's auth-adapter aggressively retried auth calls in a failure path and surfaced them as 5xx/429 when the auth-svc timed out. That behavior amplified retries and increased p99 latency.
- Customer impact: roughly 12–18 minutes of elevated 5xx/429 with p99 latency spikes to ~2.4s, peak error rate ~18% for the tenant (then reduced to ~2% post-mitigation). No data loss; degraded ingestion throughput.
- Actions completed: tenant short-circuit to 401 mapping, tenant token-throttle, routing fallback, and temporary circuit-breaker. FinSight validated client clocks and pushed a fix.
- Next permanent actions (owners & ETA):
  1) Mapping: convert token validation failure classes to 401/403 at edge to prevent retries (owner: infra/runtime, ETA: 2 weeks).
  2) Circuit-breaker defaults: add tenant-level retry ceilings to avoid amplification (owner: serving-runtime, ETA: 3 weeks).
  3) Observability: add a dedicated metric for 'auth_validation_misclassification' and an alert (owner: observability, ETA: 1 week).
  4) Customer comms and credit discussion (owner: CS/legal/sales — Marissa/Laureen), update SLA postmortem to include Dedicated pool escalation steps (ETA: 5 business days).

Tom — appreciate the clear data and patience. We'll schedule a short postmortem with SRE/infra/CS this week and share the incident report and timeline.

—Lauren
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
